column1: # Exact expected divergences discovered while relating the independent local
# Prolog semantics to the executable PLeaTTa machine. Values are ordered and
# normalized by the same parser used for the corpus differential.
# Every bounded divergence must retain a same-budget successful control, so a
# future budget reduction fails the characterization instead of weakening it.

column12: note
pinned PeTTa normalizes source True and true to the same Prolog atom before local clause matching; PLeaTTa preserves the same ordered duplicate-sensitive behavior
native and PLeaTTa independently copy each residual template; the two solution variables remain distinct
copying must preserve repeated-variable sharing within each individual solution
pinned PeTTa and the exact executable Prolog resolver both retain and unify a repeated clause variable receiving the same typed-host NaN
pinned PeTTa distinguishes the source atom #nil from the empty list (); PLeaTTa preserves their exact ordered results and multiplicity with a source-unforgeable internal nil sentinel

pinned partial(Fun,Args) is a compound distinct from the ordinary source list [partial,Fun,Args]; PLeaTTa preserves that distinction with a tagged non-list compound erased only at user-visible decoding
car-atom applied to a partial value observes no compound child and yields PeTTa's empty-list fallback rather than exposing the private representation
cdr-atom applied to a partial value yields PeTTa's empty-list fallback rather than exposing the private representation
size-atom rejects a partial value as a non-list compound on both engines

pinned PeTTa and the rebuilt executable both bind the variable clause pattern, remove and commit to the first unifying occurrence, preserve the later occurrence in source order, and expose the selected binding

raw Prolog assertion alone does not register a MeTTa head, but after add-atom registers the same name both clause kinds share one ordered predicate and the surviving raw clause prevents fun/1 unregistration
a decoded missing retract pattern takes the explicit false fallback on both engines, preserves the world, and keeps the continuation live

the same answer-then-recursion predicate returns its first answer through once/1 on both engines at the exact semantic budget used by the catch divergence witness, isolating the blocking catch macro rather than insufficient fuel

pinned and PLeaTTa streaming catch/3 both expose the first protected-goal answer to outer once/1 before the later recursive alternative diverges; this exact-budget guard rejects restoration of the former blocking catch macro or loss of the protected answer at the typed exit boundary

pinned PeTTa and PLeaTTa keep a protected-goal cut local to catch/3: the explicit cut barrier is consumed while the persistent catch delimiter survives to deliver selected, and the caller's outer alternative remains available afterward
the answer-then-recursion predicate returns its first answer through once/1 on both engines at the exact semantic budget used by the repaired case-with-Empty streaming witness

pinned and PLeaTTa expose the positive case-with-Empty answer before a later recursive scrutinee alternative diverges; this is the executable guard for the historical BISIM.softcut_macro_prefix FAIL and rejects restoration of the former blocking single-softcut lowering
the positive case lane preserves exact source order and duplicate multiplicity across distinct ordinary committed arms
failure of the first selected arm resumes the positive scrutinee search, while the Empty fallback remains suppressed because the guard has a solution
a failing scrutinee selects the source Empty fallback through re-executed negation-as-failure
a successful guard suppresses the Empty fallback even when its selected arm later fails
both failed positive execution and the negated guard discard their local binding before the Empty arm runs
a single persistent guard effect yields one visible occurrence on both engines and controls the re-execution witness
pinned case-with-Empty re-executes a failed effectful guard under negation; both persistent effects survive in exact order before fallback
a root-query cut prunes the caller's later superpose alternative on both engines
a guard-side cut in case without Empty remains at caller scope and prunes the later alternative
the positive case-with-Empty guard is caller-cut-transparent rather than hidden by the negation fallback's private barrier
a selected case arm cut prunes both retained positive-lane answers and the caller's later alternative
a cut in a nested predicate commits only that activation and leaves the root caller's later alternative reachable
the genuine translator.pl T356/T368 star-if sites stream every duplicate direct type proof instead of committing to the first proof as ordinary if-then would
